titel: Filling in the capital income annex (Anlage KAP)
kurz: When capital income has to go into the tax return, when declaring it pays off because it brings money back, and how to read the form.

bloecke.md:
Withholding at source is convenient, but it regularly leads to the wrong amount of tax. The bank only takes into account the securities account, the exemption order (Freistellungsauftrag) and the loss offset pots held with it. It does not know your taxable income, nor the second account with a neobroker or the acquisition costs of a legacy holding that was transferred without data. The amount it withholds is therefore based on incomplete information, and the gaps almost always work against the investor.

The **capital income annex (Anlage KAP)** is the form used to correct this withholding. It is filled in per person, so twice with joint assessment. Capital income reaches the assessment by three routes, which have to be kept clearly apart.

zeilen: Income that was not subject to German withholding
Mandatory. The income is assessed and taxed at 25% after the fact.
Review of the tax withheld in the case of an unused lump-sum allowance, losses at another bank, a substitute tax base or withholding tax
Application. The special rate remains; only the tax base is corrected.
Application. The capital income is taxed under the standard schedule if that is more favourable.

bloecke.md:
The first route is mandatory. Income without German withholding must be declared. This includes income from a securities account with a broker that has no German paying agent, interest from a private loan and income from fund units held abroad, for which there is a separate **investment fund income annex (Anlage KAP-INV)**. Church members who have lodged a blocking notice (Sperrvermerk) with the Federal Central Tax Office against the automatic deduction of church tax must also declare the church tax on capital income after the fact. This saves nothing; the church tax simply falls due later. If exemption orders have been spread beyond the maximum total, the investor must likewise declare the amount exempted in excess so that it is taxed after the fact.

## Most-favourable assessment

The flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) is a special rate and is not automatically more favourable than normal income tax. 25% plus solidarity surcharge comes to 26.375%. This rate applies regardless of whether the investor also earns a salary of €20,000 or €200,000. The comparison covers the tax including solidarity surcharge and church tax (Section 32d(6) EStG). At a marginal tax rate of around 25%, no solidarity surcharge is due on income tax under the schedule because of the exemption threshold (Freigrenze). Without church tax, the standard schedule is therefore more favourable as long as the personal marginal tax rate is below 26.375%, and in any case at a rate below 25%. This affects more people than is often assumed, for example students with a part-time job, pensioners with a small pension, parents on parental leave, self-employed people in a loss year and anyone who takes a longer unpaid break during a year.

The [[Most-favourable assessment (Günstigerprüfung)|most-favourable assessment (Günstigerprüfung)]] is applied for with a cross in line 4. It applies uniformly to all capital income for the year and only for that one year. Taxing dividends under the schedule and interest at the flat rate is therefore not possible. For income tax, the application has no disadvantage, because the tax office calculates both variants and applies the lower one. The saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) is retained. However, actual income-related expenses (Werbungskosten) may not be deducted even when taxation is under the schedule (Section 20(9) EStG).

bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation in euros with amounts after the saver's allowance, excluding church tax and excluding solidarity surcharge on the tax under the schedule, which usually does not apply because of the exemption threshold. The break-even point is therefore 26.375%.

bloecke.titel: Side effects of the most-favourable assessment
bloecke.md: Besides the tax liability, the application also changes the **total amount of income (Gesamtbetrag der Einkünfte)** shown in the tax assessment notice, because the capital income is then included in it. If the notice is presented elsewhere, it shows higher income there. This affects, for example, the health insurance fund for voluntary members, the parental allowance office (Elterngeldstelle), the student grant office (BAföG-Amt), the housing benefit office (Wohngeldstelle) and maintenance calculations. The tax office does not check these consequences; its comparison looks only at income tax.

## Review of the tax withheld

Line 5 is used to apply for a review of the tax withheld. In practice, this route is needed most often. The special rate remains unchanged; only what the bank could not know is corrected. Six cases cover almost everything:

1. The saver's allowance was not used. Without an exemption order, the bank withholds tax from the first cent. The allowance is not lost as a result; it is granted retrospectively in the assessment.
2. Losses arose at one bank and gains at another. They are only brought together via the tax return and only with the loss certificate (Verlustbescheinigung), which must be applied for by 15 December of the loss year (Section 43a(3) sentences 4 and 5 EStG).
3. The bank applied a **substitute tax base (Ersatzbemessungsgrundlage)**. If it lacks the acquisition data, it taxes a flat 30% of the sale proceeds (Section 43a(2) EStG), regardless of how large the gain was. Investors who still have the old contract notes correct this here and often get four-figure sums back.
4. Foreign withholding tax could no longer be used in the bank's withholding tax pot (Quellensteuertopf) because the income was exempt anyway (Section 32d(5) EStG).
5. The bank withheld tax on the advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale) in January, but the exemption order was only given in February. The order applies to the whole calendar year, and as long as no tax certificate (Steuerbescheinigung) has been issued, the bank must correct the withholding itself (Section 44b(5) EStG). If this has not happened, the tax is refunded in the assessment.
6. The case concerns fund units bought before 2009. For these there is a personal allowance of €100,000 on increases in value from 1 January 2018 (Section 56(6) InvStG, Investment Tax Act). The bank does not know about this allowance and never applies it. It is granted only in the assessment and carried forward annually.

Account A with a neobroker has no exemption order. Share sales there produce a gain of €3,000. The bank withholds 26.375%, that is €791.25.

Account B with the main bank has a loss of €1,200 from share sales and no gains to offset it against. The loss certificate was applied for in December.

In the assessment, the two accounts are offset: 3,000 − 1,200 = €1,800. After deducting the €1,000 saver's allowance, €800 remains. The tax is €200 plus €11 solidarity surcharge, that is €211. The refund is 791.25 − 211 = €580.25. This requires two crosses and four figures copied over.

bloecke.unter: The same example step by step, with each correction step equal to 26.375% of the respective amount.

bloecke.md:
## Structure of the form

The line numbers shift from year to year, but the structure stays the same and so makes it easier to find your way around in every year's version. The applications come first, followed by income with German withholding, income without withholding and the loss items. The taxes already paid are at the very bottom.

bloecke.titel: Structure of the capital income annex
zeilen: Most-favourable assessment, review of the tax withheld, assessment of church tax
Total capital income, gains from share sales included in it, substitute tax bases applied
separated into losses from share sales and other losses
the part already used up through exemption orders
Foreign securities account, private loan, other cases under Section 32d(3) EStG
Capital income withholding tax, solidarity surcharge, church tax
withholding tax creditable under a double taxation agreement (Section 32d(5) EStG)
Investment income that was not subject to withholding (distributions, advance lump sums, sales)
own calculation from the fund data
Annex for income from holdings (Anlage KAP-BET)
Capital income from holdings that is determined separately

bloecke.titel: The tax certificate as a template
bloecke.md: Under Section 45a(2) EStG, the paying agent must issue a certificate in the officially prescribed form on request. Many brokers only generate it on request or only make it available in the spring. Its fields are arranged in the same sections as the form. With the certificate, the figures can therefore be copied over without any calculation.

Since the return for 2017, supporting documents are no longer submitted; they only have to be kept available. You keep them until the assessment notice is final. With substitute tax bases and legacy holdings, they should be kept much longer, because there the old purchase contract notes replace evidence that nobody else can provide any more.

## Deadlines

For taxpayers who are obliged to file, the deadline for 2025 ran until 31 July 2026 (Section 149(2) AO, Fiscal Code). With a tax adviser, it runs until the end of February 2027 (Section 149(3) AO). For a voluntary return that is only meant to recover money, four years remain. This is the limitation period for assessment (Festsetzungsfrist) under Section 169(2) sentence 1 no. 2 AO. A refund earns interest of 0.15% a month, that is 1.8% a year (Section 238(1a) AO). Interest starts to accrue 15 months after the end of the tax year (Section 233a(2) AO).

bloecke.titel: Open tax years for voluntary returns
bloecke.unter: As of 19 September 2026. For a voluntary return, the end of the fourth year after the tax year is what counts.

ereignisse.text: The oldest year that is still open. After that, the limitation period has expired, and unused lump-sum allowances or loss certificates are lost for good.

The base interest rate (Basiszins) for the advance lump sum was 2.55%. However, the advance lump sum for that year was only deemed received in January 2024 and counts towards the 2024 tax year. None was deemed received in January 2023 because the base interest rate for 2022 was negative.
The Annual Tax Act 2024 (Jahressteuergesetz) abolished the loss offsetting limit for derivative transactions (Termingeschäfte). The abolition applies in all open cases, including earlier years.
For voluntary returns, there is time until 31 December 2029. Taxpayers who were obliged to file and missed the deadline face a late filing surcharge (Verspätungszuschlag).

schritte.text: Request the annual tax certificate from every bank, including for accounts without any activity. Without a bank's certificate, its details will be missing from the form later.
If it is below 25%, put a cross in line 4. If in doubt, put a cross there too, because the tax office calculates both variants.
Put a cross in line 5 if there is an unused allowance, losses at another bank, a substitute tax base or outstanding withholding tax.

The certificate is arranged in the same sections as the form. Income from foreign securities accounts goes in the capital income annex, investment fund income from them in the investment fund income annex.
Check whether the capital income withholding tax credited matches the total of all certificates. The deadline for an objection is one month from notification.

bloecke.titel: Limits of the capital income annex
bloecke.md: The capital income annex cannot be used to recover withholding tax that was withheld above the rate agreed in the double taxation agreement. That requires an application in the source country. Withholding tax incurred at fund level is not credited either; the partial exemption (Teilfreistellung) serves as flat-rate compensation for it. Income-related expenses are not taken into account, not even with the most-favourable assessment. Capital losses are also not offset against salary, rents or business income, because losses from capital assets remain restricted to their own category of income (Section 20(6) sentence 1 EStG).

mitnehmen: The bank calculates the tax withheld with incomplete information, and the missing details are added in the capital income annex.
Line 4 is used to apply for the most-favourable assessment, which pays off at a marginal tax rate below 25%, while line 5 leaves the special rate in place and only corrects the tax base.
The three most common refund cases are an unused saver's allowance, losses at a second bank and the 30% substitute tax base.
A return that only serves to obtain a refund can be filed within four years; for the 2022 tax year, the deadline ends on 31 December 2026.
The form can only be filled in with the annual tax certificate, whose fields correspond to the sections of the capital income annex.

begriffe.text: Application under Section 32d(6) EStG to have capital income taxed under the personal income tax schedule instead of at 25%. It applies uniformly to all capital income of a year, and the tax office automatically applies the more favourable variant.
Flat-rate gain of 30% of the sale proceeds that the bank uses when it lacks the acquisition data (Section 43a(2) EStG). It can only be corrected via the tax return with purchase records.

Annual certificate from the paying agent under Section 45a(2) EStG, which must be issued on request. Its fields follow the officially prescribed form and correspond to the sections of the capital income annex.
Voluntary tax return without a legal obligation, used to recover tax that was overpaid. It is possible within the four-year limitation period for assessment under Section 169(2) sentence 1 no. 2 AO.

Supplementary form for income from investment funds that was not subject to domestic withholding, typically from fund units in a foreign securities account. Distributions, the advance lump sum and capital gains have to be calculated yourself there.
